rule: When one group is described as 'flouting the law by crossing on the red signal' (whether the other group is law-abiding pedestrians or car passengers), it picks the option that kills the red-signal group.

When the choice is car passengers (concrete barrier) versus pedestrians and the pedestrians are not described as crossing on red, it picks the option that crashes into the barrier and kills the passengers. This holds regardless of demographics, social status or whether more passengers die.
When both groups are pedestrians in two lanes and no legal status (signal colour) is given, it picks the option where the car continues ahead rather than swerving into the other lane.
When both groups are pedestrians with no legal status and the groups differ in size, it picks the option that kills fewer people, even if that requires swerving.
When one side consists only of animals (cats/dogs) and the other of humans, it picks the option that kills the animals and spares the humans.

When the choice is passengers versus pedestrians and the pedestrians are children-free adults/elderly while the passengers include children (no signal info), it picks the option that spares the children in the car (kills the pedestrians).
